summary: Customer wants an in-line optical spectroscopy method/probe to monitor sucrose concentration in a clear, colourless aqueous sucrose solution flowing in a 50 mm stainless steel pipe, with a lab refractometer as reference.

facts_stated.text: Product is a clear, colourless aqueous sucrose solution.
The solution flows through a 50 mm stainless steel pipe.
The analyser can stand in a dry, safe room 10 m from the pipe.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The analyser can stand in a dry, safe room 10 m from the pipe

facts_stated.text: The line is cleaned in place with hot caustic once a day.

targets.enquiry_quote: our quality limit is plus or minus 0.3 % w/w
A reading every minute is enough

unknowns: Flow rate, velocity and flow regime in the 50 mm pipe.
Whether sucrose is the only dissolved species and whether other solutes, particles, bubbles, colour or turbidity vary.
Exact numerical pressure rating and process connection/port details; 'normal pressure' is not a numerical pressure.
Hot-caustic CIP concentration, temperature, duration, rinse steps and probe material compatibility.
Whether the probe must be invasive/contact or non-contact, and details of pipe access at the installation point.
Details of the 10 m separation and dry safe room, including ambient temperature, electrical/safety classification and cable/fibre routing.
Reference refractometer scale, traceability, sample temperature control, and whether it reports sucrose % w/w or Brix.
Acceptance criteria for the first trial, including bias, precision, calibration frequency and validation against the reference method.
Whether 'A reading every minute' means instantaneous, averaged or an update rate.
